headline: Bangladesh Transforms Banana Waste Into Gold
meta_description: Bangladesh is turning banana plant stems into profitable textiles and handicrafts, with potential to earn $94 million annually in exports.
summary_short: Bangladeshi entrepreneurs are converting banana plant waste into valuable fiber for textiles, handicrafts, and eco-friendly products—generating millions in export potent…
body:
Bangladesh is quietly unlocking a fortune hidden in its banana plants. The country's agricultural byproduct—fiber extracted from banana stems—is being transformed into textiles, handicrafts, sarees, bags, and mats that command premium prices on global markets. A 2024 study reveals the scale of this opportunity: if commercialized effectively, Bangladesh could produce around 37,800 tons of banana fiber annually and generate more than $94 million in annual export earnings. Today, the country earns roughly $1.5 million from banana fiber exports—leaving vast untapped potential on the table. The math is compelling: banana fiber sells for more than double the price of jute fiber, Bangladesh's traditional textile export, yet it costs less to produce because it uses agricultural waste rather than requiring dedicated cultivation.

Entrepreneurs across the country are already scaling up. Md Hafijul Islam, owner of New Bhai Bhai Engineering Workshop near Dhaka, collects fiber from 250 producers and exports to China while supporting a network of over 1,000 local women who braid fiber at home for extra income. Parveen Akhter, based in the southwestern district of Narail, extracts fiber from banana stems collected from nearby orchards, selling it to export buyers for 500 to 600 takas per kilogram. Companies like Banana Fiber BD, EcoFiber BD, and Modern Banana Fiber Company Ltd. are expanding production to meet global demand for sustainable materials.

The main challenge remains technology. While entrepreneurs initially used locally made machines, these often produce lower-quality fiber, limiting prices. Machine modernization and standardization across the sector could unlock the full potential. Bangladesh already produces roughly 813,600 tons of bananas annually across 54,756 hectares—generating 3.78 million tons of biomass annually, of which about 1 percent can be extracted as valuable fiber. For rural communities and small manufacturers, this waste has become opportunity.
quick_facts: Bangladesh could earn $94 million annually from banana fiber exports if sector scales
Banana fiber sells for more than double the price of jute fiber
EcoFiber BD supplies 100 tons of fiber monthly from network of 1,000+ entrepreneurs
Md Hafijul Islam supports 1,000+ local women earning income through fiber braiding at home
